requirements.description: Three server-authoritative symbol dice implement six coverage targets and transparent one-, two-, and three-hit net payouts.
requirements.notes: Issue #77 allocates the permanent distinct rules requirement for issue #133. Issue #1035 preserves every symbol, hit-count, and payout rule while moving only browser route ownership and unchanged presentation declarations onto the shared lifecycle and external stylesheet.

requirements.description: Authenticated sessions own private reload-safe rounds, settled history, and canonical route restoration.
requirements.notes: Session context overrides caller player ids; provider-current prepared faces remain private until exact ledger proof allows one terminal result to survive reload and process restart. The shared route generation rejects stale initial-state and delayed-settlement responses after teardown or remount.

requirements.description: Aggregate symbol wagers and returned credits use the shared ledger exactly once under durable request identities.
requirements.notes: SimpleWagerGame owns the aggregate debit, optional returned credit, proof recovery, and conflicting-retry refusal; no game code mutates balances directly.

requirements.description: Crown and Anchor supplies complete English and Russian responsive, accessible, reduced-motion-safe, timer-clean play with all three dice and all six symbol hit-result panels painted and contained at every governed viewport.
requirements.notes: Evidence covers both locales and every governed viewport; BR-CAA-001 rejects any missing, unpainted, or stage-escaped die or symbol panel, requires the external stylesheet singleton, preserves the dominant stage and control sizes, and proves teardown plus remount without stale route DOM.

requirements.description: Catalog, contract, browser, long-suite, and formal TEST-092 discovery include Crown and Anchor with requirement, module, version, visual, and essential-stage traceability.
requirements.notes: Descriptor sort order 210 and the catalog-discovered long driver are canonical; listener-free lifecycle evidence rejects duplicate route helpers or CSS owners, and formal evidence rejects incomplete Crown and Anchor theater even when no enabled control is clipped.

requirements.description: Every Crown and Anchor settled-history publication compares its detached game-owned baseline with provider-current state, preserves unrelated sibling fields, accepts an identical result idempotently, and rejects a stale different writer before it can overwrite the authoritative round journal.
requirements.notes: The SimpleWagerGame lifecycle adapter owns each provider-current transition without a detached whole-document saver. Multiworker activation stays blocked because wallet and game-state publication remain separate durable boundaries.

requirements.description: Crown and Anchor delegates its prepared wager, committed-face recovery, optional returned-credit movement, replay lookup, lifecycle finalization, and provider-current history publication to one SimpleWagerGame coordinator while preserving the frozen v1 client_request_id, caa_ round identity, direct oldest-to-newest one-hundred-round history, public round, active-state privacy, and historical ledger evidence semantics.
requirements.notes: The game service contains exactly one SimpleWagerGame construction and no direct GameSettlementGateway, CoreLedgerGateway, apply_once call, or game-local settlement lock. Canonical proof fields remain beside the legacy idempotency_key compatibility field without changing the frozen v1 contract.
